source_note: Chinese hot-topic candidates are collected from public trend pages; English wording is matched to supplied official English headlines when possible, otherwise suggested neutrally.

topics.chinese_topic: 不满房东涨租 于东来自掏65亿建商场
topics.official_english: Retail tycoon Yu Donglai builds his own mall with 6.5 billion yuan after rent dispute
topics.why_hot: Yu Donglai, founder of the popular Chinese retail chain Pangdonglai, reportedly spent 6.5 billion yuan of his own money to build a shopping mall after being unhappy with a rent increase. The story resonates with public sentiment about high commercial rents and the influence of a successful entrepreneur.
topics.share_angle: This story can be used to discuss retail economics, landlord-tenant dynamics, and Yu Donglai's reputation as a people-focused businessman. It highlights how a business owner reacted to a common pressure point, offering a lens into Chinese consumer culture and entrepreneurship.

topics.chinese_topic: 上海降水量破纪录 学生舍不得点外卖
topics.official_english: Shanghai sees record rainfall, students hesitate to order takeout
topics.why_hot: Shanghai experienced record-breaking rainfall, and a touching detail emerged that some students chose not to order takeout out of concern for delivery riders. This sparked warm discussions about empathy and extreme weather.
topics.share_angle: This is a relatable human-interest story that can lead into broader topics such as extreme weather events in China, the gig economy, and social kindness during difficult conditions.

topics.chinese_topic: 新能源车为何越造越大
topics.official_english: Why are new energy vehicles getting bigger?
topics.why_hot: A trending debate about the growing size of new energy vehicles (NEVs) in China. This connects to consumer preferences, battery technology, and automotive design trends.
topics.share_angle: An opportunity to explain the market logic behind larger EVs: bigger batteries for longer range, shifting consumer tastes, and the implications for urban parking and infrastructure.

topics.chinese_topic: 豆包回应“推荐酒店抽取12%佣金”
topics.official_english: AI assistant Doubao responds to claims of a 12% commission on hotel recommendations
topics.why_hot: Doubao, a popular Chinese AI assistant, addressed allegations that it takes a 12% commission when recommending hotels. This raised questions about AI monetization and the impartiality of AI-generated suggestions.
topics.share_angle: This is highly relevant to global conversations about AI ethics, sponsored content, and the business models of AI assistants. It can be framed around transparency and user trust.

topics.chinese_topic: 朱雀三号遥二运载火箭发射推迟
topics.official_english: Zhuque-3 Y2 carrier rocket launch postponed
topics.why_hot: The Zhuque-3 Y2, a reusable rocket developed by Chinese private company LandSpace, had its launch postponed. This attracted attention from space enthusiasts and observers of China's commercial space industry.
topics.share_angle: This can serve as a quick update on China's private spaceflight efforts and the technical hurdles in developing reusable rockets, as postponements are normal in the industry.

topics.official_english: Museums adopt 'no reservation unless necessary' policy
topics.why_hot: Discussion about Chinese museums encouraging visitors to visit without advanced reservations unless necessary. This is part of a broader effort to make museums more accessible and reduce bureaucracy.
topics.share_angle: A good topic for discussing cultural access, tourism policies, and how museums balance visitor flow with the convenience of the public.

topics.chinese_topic: 从一笔账单看60万亿消费KPI的底气
topics.official_english: A single bill reveals confidence in the 60 trillion yuan consumption KPI
topics.why_hot: This topic uses an individual spending example to illustrate why China can be confident about reaching a consumption target of 60 trillion yuan. It resonates with the public as an economic discussion grounded in everyday life.
topics.share_angle: This can be explained as a window into China's consumption patterns, domestic demand outlook, and how economic goals are communicated through relatable examples.

topics.chinese_topic: 商场负一层遭积水倒灌 展厅车漂走
topics.official_english: Water pours into mall basement, showroom cars float away
topics.why_hot: During heavy rain, a shopping mall's basement floor flooded and cars on display in a showroom were seen floating away. The dramatic scene quickly drew attention, highlighting the severity of urban flooding.
topics.share_angle: A striking example of extreme weather's impact on cities. This can be used to discuss climate adaptation, urban infrastructure resilience, and the challenges cities face with heavy rainfall.
